item.title: US tightens AI chip export controls to deter Chinese companies from accessing compute remotely
item.description: Background The U.S. Commerce Department is rolling out an interim rule designed to close loopholes in existing export restrictions. Previously, rules required licenses only for shipping chips directly to companies in embargoed countries like China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea. However, companies have increasingly turned to remote-access loopholes, using overseas data centers to train advanced models. Key Details The new rule applies to any data center or network exceeding a specific computing power metric of 12 million total processing performance, roughly equivalent to about 750 Nvidia H100 or H200 chips. Operators must obtain licenses within 90 days if they serve customers from restricted countries. Additionally, the rule introduces new licensing requirements for semiconductor transfers to Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand, and Brazil due to a higher risk of diversion, though chips destined for U.S.-based companies in these nations are exempt. The framework also rescinds the previous administration's AI Diffusion Rule. Industry Impact This regulatory shift forces global cloud and data center operators to strictly monitor customer ownership structures and network access. It comes in the wake of heightened scrutiny over Chinese firms scrambling for overseas compute capacity and aims to block actors from leveraging U.S. advanced semiconductors for intelligence-related or military activities.

item.title: Biogen inks $411M neurodegeneration pact with protein degrader biotech TrimTech
item.description: Collaboration Details Biogen has entered into a biobucks agreement with U.K.-based TrimTech worth up to $411 million, which includes $32 million in upfront and research milestone payments. Under the pact, Biogen secures an exclusive global license to small molecule protein degraders developed through TrimTech's proprietary platform. Technology and Targets TrimTech focuses on using the E3-ligase TRIM21 to clear disease-causing protein aggregates. Its approach features bispecific chimeric molecules called TRIMTAC and mutual binding facilitator TRIMGLUE, offering an alternative to standard PROTACs. The company targets neurodegenerative conditions such as Huntington’s, Alzheimer’s, and Parkinson’s. Industry Context Founded in 2023, TrimTech previously raised a $47 million seed round involving major players like Johnson & Johnson, Eli Lilly, and Pfizer. This new agreement reinforces the growing interest from major drugmakers in targeted protein degradation for challenging diseases.

item.title: AI model detects small fires and smoke in PV plants
item.description: Background While deep learning has been widely applied in photovoltaic (PV) inspections for crack detection and hot-spot localization, dedicated fire detection in PV environments has rarely been explored. Details and Performance Developed by China Huaneng Group, the system integrates a custom annotated corpus named PV-Fire, which contains 5,824 images gathered from operating utility-scale plants and controlled outdoor burns. Based on the YOLOv12 model, the framework incorporates a patch-aware attention block, a multi-level gather-and-distribute mechanism, and an adaptive fusion head to spot weak flames and tiny smoke plumes. In benchmarks, PVFire-YOLO reached an mAP@50 of 87.4% on its native dataset, lowered the reflection-related false-positive rate down to 3.1%, and ran at 79 frames per second on a desktop GPU. Outlook The researchers state that future work will expand the image corpus to cover diverse climates, introduce temporal filtering to minimize isolated false positives, and combine visible light detection with infrared thermal imaging.

item.title: Novo’s CagriSema drives more than 20% weight loss at lower doses
item.description: Clinical Trial Results Novo Nordisk reported data from the Phase 3 REDEFINE 9 trial at the ObesityWeek 2026 conference. Patients receiving weekly doses of 1 mg and 1.7 mg of CagriSema lost 21% and 20.7% of their body weight, respectively, at week 68. These findings demonstrate that meaningful efficacy can be achieved below the previously studied highest dose. Background and Market Context CagriSema combines the amylin analog cagrilintide and the GLP-1 receptor agonist semaglutide. Earlier data from the REDEFINE 1 trial showed 22.7% weight loss at higher doses, which initially disappointed investors who had expected even higher figures. Despite previous setbacks, including failing to beat Eli Lilly’s Zepbound in a head-to-head test, Novo Nordisk continues to position the drug as a major next-generation therapy. Regulatory Outlook and Tolerability The latest findings form part of a broader data presentation as the drug awaits a U.S. FDA decision expected by the end of 2026. Analysts noted that tolerability remained consistent with previous studies, showing common side effects such as nausea and vomiting, while the company prepares to leverage its extensive clinical data to enter the market.

item.title: University spin-out turns internal lab tool into JetForge 3D printer
item.description: Background and Origins Founded by Richard Hague, Chris Tuck, and Ricky Wildman, Added started as a contract research business to handle industrial projects that did not fit a traditional academic schedule. Over time, the team focused on material jetting and binder jetting, building custom equipment when commercial prototyping machines proved too restrictive for testing new inks. The JetForge Platform Commercial 3D printers often lock users into a single manufacturer's materials, while typical development systems can be difficult to operate and maintain. JetForge solves this by packing the driver board, recirculation pump, and printhead into a removable module called a Blade. Users can swap these modules or run different heads simultaneously, configuring the machine for specific experimental needs such as multi-material printing or droplet inspection. Applications and Outlook The founders see immediate opportunities in electronics, such as printing conductive circuits directly through the body of polymer components or onto wearables. Added also collaborates with industrial partners on projects like desalination filter spacers and pharmaceutical oral dosage forms, aiming to help researchers quickly test and customize new materials.

item.title: Flatiron Energy starts construction on a massive 1.2GWh battery storage project in Massachusetts
item.description: Project Overview US energy storage developer Flatiron Energy has officially broken ground on the Energizar Energy Storage Project in Chelsea, Massachusetts. Flatiron states that the facility will feature a capacity of 250MW/1,200MWh, making it the largest battery energy storage system in the Northeast and one of the largest urban BESS facilities globally. Financing and Construction In October, Flatiron secured approximately US$850 million in financing for the project, covering construction loans, term loans, equity commitments, and tax credit transfers. Consigli Construction Co. is leading the construction work, with commercial operations scheduled to begin in the fourth quarter of 2027. Local Impact and Grid Role The facility aims to support the Greater Boston region by storing electricity during low-demand periods and releasing it during peak hours to improve grid reliability. Additionally, Flatiron is investing in local green economy programs, workforce development, and providing emergency response training for the local fire department.

item.title: Eli Lilly secures 1.5 billion dollar deal for Calytrix Bio to expand blood cancer pipeline
item.description: Eli Lilly is further expanding its footprint in the treatment of rare blood cancers by striking a deal worth up to $1.5 billion for Calytrix Bio, a biotech founded by J.P. Morgan's life sciences venture capital arm. The acquisition centers on a preclinical biparatopic antibody designed to target mutant calreticulin, which drives conditions like essential thrombocythemia and myelofibrosis. Unlike current therapies that primarily manage symptoms, this approach aims to provide disease-modifying activity. Citi analysts noted that the asset strategically complements Lilly's existing pipeline assets, though they cautioned that the program is still in the preclinical stage and faces a high safety bar. This transaction caps off a busy year of multibillion-dollar acquisitions and licensing agreements for Lilly, fueled largely by the strong sales of its GLP-1 drugs.

item.title: Canada pitches its biotech sector to Europe as U.S. political uncertainty grows
item.description:
U.S. political instability and uncertainty surrounding institutions like the FDA and NIH have prompted Canadian biotechs and contract research organizations to look beyond the United States. According to industry representatives at the BIO-Europe conference in Cologne, Germany, Canadian firms are actively promoting their strengths to European partners, aiming to secure licensing deals, co-development partners, and clinical collaborations.
On the opening day of the conference, three Canadian and Belgian health organizations—BioQuébec, Bioscience Association Manitoba (BAM), and BioWin—signed a trilateral Memorandum of Understanding to boost business development and knowledge exchange. Industry stakeholders note that Canada offers distinct advantages, including 30-day clinical trial application reviews by Health Canada, tax incentives, and a strong presence in emerging fields like AI-driven drug discovery and cell therapies.

item.title: Altera, OQC and NVIDIA Link Quantum Processor to GPU Computing
item.description: Background As quantum computers grow in scale, the number of qubits is increasing much faster than the physical space available for the traditional control equipment around them. This creates a bottleneck where control hardware needs to become significantly denser. Details According to Altera, the new end-to-end reference design is built on an Agilex 9 Direct RF FPGA. The FPGA handles real-time system control, qubit initialization, and resonator readout, communicating directly with an OQC quantum processing unit through specialized RF electronics. Meanwhile, NVIDIA NVQLink connects the FPGA to NVIDIA GPUs, which take over heavy computational tasks such as system calibration and machine learning-based readout classification using CUDA. Impact This collaboration provides developers with a validated software stack and a built-in emulation path to test algorithms before physical hardware is ready. The system is scheduled for a live demonstration at Supercomputing 2026 in Chicago, with the commercial release expected in January 2027.

item.title: Can Robots Bring Stroke Surgery to Remote Hospitals?
item.description:
Remedy Robotics was founded by clinician David Bell and engineer Jake Sganga to tackle a stark medical reality: only about 1 in 10 eligible patients receive mechanical thrombectomies for acute ischemic strokes, largely because life-saving procedures are concentrated in major urban centers. Traditional stroke surgery requires physicians to manually thread a wire and catheter through narrow blood vessels while relying solely on a flat, two-dimensional X-ray, making it a blind and physically demanding task.
To bridge this gap, Remedy developed the N1 System, which features a steerable catheter driven by a robotic arm and guided by computer-vision software. The system translates basic directional commands from a controller into precise movements while overlaying 3D CT scans onto X-ray feeds. After successful preliminary tests on silicone models and a small nonemergency human trial in Toronto, the company recently secured $62 million in funding to advance upcoming clinical trials within the University of California system.
Despite the technological progress, widespread adoption of telesurgery faces steep hurdles. Experts point out that successful remote operations depend heavily on reliable network infrastructure, as rural areas often suffer from high latency that can disrupt surgical timing. Additionally, smaller hospitals frequently lack the necessary on-site medical staff, specialized intensive care units, and supporting equipment needed to handle complex stroke emergencies safely.

item.title: Google Maps updates Ask Maps with travel planning and local appointment booking
item.description:
According to Google AI:
According to Google Maps Product Director Maz Khorasani, the latest update introduces several conversational capabilities designed for holiday travel and preparation. Itinerary Building and Route Tips Users can now build step-by-step trip itineraries by prompting Ask Maps, which generates day-by-day schedules with numbered map pins. These plans can be shared or exported to Google Docs. When heading out, users can view live traffic, business hours, and weather conditions, and dynamically add stops such as scenic viewpoints along the route. Additionally, new route tips provide information on parking, EV charging, tolls, and delays. Appointment Booking and List Search Leveraging new agentic capabilities, Ask Maps can search online and call local businesses to find available appointments for services like pet care, beauty, and auto repair. Furthermore, users can query their saved lists with specific constraints, such as finding a saved restaurant that can seat five people within the next 30 minutes. Availability and Regional Rollout These updates began rolling out on Android and iOS on November 16, 2026. Ask Maps is also expanding to 30 European countries, including Spain, Germany, and the U.K., bringing availability to over 200 countries and territories. While travel itineraries and list search are available globally, the 'know before you go' route tips and appointment-finding features are launching first in the U.S.

item.title: Helus' Psychedelic Depression Drug Succeeds in Phase 3 Trial But Faces Safety Scrutiny
item.description:
Helus Pharma announced that its psychedelic drug candidate, HLP003, showed positive results in a Phase 3 clinical trial for major depression. In the study, participants received one dose on the first day and a second dose three weeks later alongside standard antidepressants. At six weeks, the treatment group achieved a 19.5-point reduction on the MADRS depression rating scale, compared to an 11.9-point reduction in the placebo group. At 12 weeks, the effect was largely sustained, with a 16.9-point reduction for the treatment group versus 9.9 points for the placebo group, with all differences being statistically significant.
Despite the promising efficacy data, the trial recorded a number of serious adverse events. These safety concerns have raised questions regarding the risk-benefit profile of utilizing psychedelics for psychiatric conditions, a therapeutic avenue currently being explored by multiple companies in the biotechnology sector.

item.title: Materialise Calls for Coordinated Defence Additive Manufacturing Network in Europe
item.description:
Speaking at the AM Innovation and Standards Summit at Formnext 2026, Materialise CTO Bart Van der Schueren argued that Europe's existing additive manufacturing expertise and industrial capacity are currently underutilized as a cohesive defence capability.
Instead of treating 3D printing merely as a quick fix for isolated spare parts or emergency supply chain disruptions, the company suggests that the defence sector should recognize it as a flexible and scalable production capacity. Achieving this vision requires European governments and institutions to establish common frameworks across companies and national borders.
Materialise stresses that shared approaches to standards, qualification, security, digital production processes, and the harmonization of export control regulations are essential prerequisites for connecting individual production resources into a reliable, distributed manufacturing network.

item.title: SAP and Infosys Executives Discuss Scaling AI Agents Across the Enterprise
item.description:
Enterprise AI is shifting from isolated proofs of concept to autonomous agents running core business processes. However, industry data shows that the vast majority of organizations remain stuck in pilot mode. According to Thorsten Leiduck of SAP and Satinder Pal Singh of Infosys, this bottleneck stems from treating AI as a department-level technology initiative rather than an operating model transformation.
To bridge this gap, executives recommend evaluating use cases through three lenses: impact, feasibility, and scalability. Furthermore, companies must build a connected, semantically rich data layer to ensure high accuracy in mission-critical operations like supply chains and financial closes. Finally, integrated governance tools—such as SAP's Agent Hub—are required to maintain trust, security, and oversight as digital coworkers take on greater responsibilities.

item.title: Alibaba Launches Qwen4-Max AI Model With Focus on Security
item.description: Background Alibaba has launched Qwen4-Max as the successor to Qwen3.8-Max, aiming to capture complex professional and scientific tasks across various industries such as finance, healthcare, and 3D modeling. Performance and Cost According to Alibaba, Qwen4-Max outperforms its predecessor in nearly every evaluated capability while reducing token usage. In their Work360 evaluation, the average cost per task dropped significantly from $4.43 to $1.67, representing a 62 percent reduction, largely driven by optimized cached inputs. Security Enhancements Following past scrutiny regarding model behavior, Alibaba focused heavily on security for this release. The company claims that Qwen4-Max showed improved function-level pass rates in security testing and strengthened safeguards against cybersecurity misuse by removing offensive attack data from training sets while retaining defensive capabilities.

item.title: CityUHK Develops High-Fidelity Lunar Regolith Simulant to Support National Lunar Missions
item.description: Background Lunar regolith is a critical resource for space exploration, but real samples returned by missions like Chang'e are extremely limited. Traditional simulants made from Earth minerals often contain impurities and differ in microstructures due to varying environmental conditions, which can lead to experimental deviations. Details Supported by the Innovation and Technology Commission since April 2025, the CityUHK team has collaborated with the Qian Xuesen Laboratory of Space Technology under CAST. Using a hydrolysis method, the team precisely controlled the chemical composition, mineral proportions, and crystal structure based on Chang'e-5 samples. They successfully fabricated four key lunar minerals and amorphous matter, creating a 3D-printable simulant. Impact This high-fidelity simulant helps engineers better understand thermal and chemical properties while improving the design of lunar rovers and construction materials. It minimizes space mission risks and offers a valuable reference for exploring other celestial bodies like Mars.

item.title: Yixing Communication files for Hong Kong IPO: Revenue grows, but profit fluctuates and chip prices plummet
item.description: Background Shanghai Yixing Communication Technology Co., Ltd. has submitted its prospectus for a Hong Kong IPO. According to the data cited from the Frost & Sullivan report, the company ranks third globally in the cellular communication chip market with a 3.9% market share, and its revenue grew at a compound annual growth rate of 13.72% from 2023 to 2025. Key Details Despite rising revenues, the company's profitability fluctuates heavily. It recorded a net profit only in 2024 out of a three-and-a-half-year reporting period, with cumulative losses reaching 201.12 million yuan. In addition, its business relies heavily on a few partners, with the top five customers contributing over 75% of revenue and top five suppliers accounting for over 80% of procurement. On the product side, the average selling prices of both NB-IoT and Cat.1bis chips dropped significantly, with Cat.1bis chip prices falling by nearly 48% by the first half of 2026 compared to 2023, causing chip gross margins to plummet. Impact While facing continuous price wars and heavy reliance on major clients and suppliers, the company maintains high research and development investments, totaling over 520 million yuan across the reporting period. The ongoing paradox of heavy R&D spending alongside shrinking product profitability poses serious challenges for its upcoming public listing.

item.title: APEC CEOs urge common AI safeguards to boost trade
item.description:
Ahead of the Apec CEO summit in Shenzhen, Deloitte released a report based on a survey of 1,278 executives across 18 Apec economies and India. According to Deloitte's Asia-Pacific CEO Robert Hillard, cross-border coordination is vital because over 70 percent of global trade originates, ends, or takes place within the region.
The survey highlights that about half of the respondents view cybersecurity and risk frameworks as the top priority for regional cooperation, while 44 percent call for collaborative investment in digital infrastructure. Furthermore, Deloitte China CEO Dora Liu noted that other economies can learn from Shenzhen by integrating AI with real-world industrial capabilities.
The report also shows that more than half of surveyed executives rank AI as their top priority, surpassing revenue growth. Chinese enterprises lead this adoption curve, with 78 percent deploying AI across multiple functions, driven largely by the integration of physical AI into the country's manufacturing sector.

item.title: Elon Musk and 165,000 others sign open letter asking Nvidia to bring back Jensen Huang
item.description:
Following Jensen Huang's resignation after a 33-year tenure at Nvidia due to a personal conduct scandal, a massive pushback has emerged from Silicon Valley. An open letter demanding his reinstatement has gathered over 165,000 signatures, including prominent figures like Elon Musk, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, and Y Combinator president Garry Tan. Supporters argue that while Huang made personal mistakes, his contributions to the company and the broader AI industry are irreplaceable.
However, Washington is taking a starkly different stance. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated that Nvidia needs a dramatic shake-up and should look outside the company for its next leader. Bessent also raised serious national security concerns, demanding answers within 10 days regarding whether Nvidia knowingly allowed its most advanced AI chips to reach China, pointing to Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that bought nearly $5 billion in hardware and is linked to the scandal.
Meanwhile, analysts remain skeptical about a potential comeback. Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives described the petition as a distraction, noting that external candidates or interim CEO Colette Kress are much more viable options for moving forward. Huang has reportedly agreed to appear before US congressional committees to address these mounting questions.

item.title: The business of artificial intimacy in the age of loneliness
item.description:
As loneliness grows, virtual companion apps like Urvashi, Saathiya, and Meetra are rapidly gaining popularity by offering users instant emotional validation, reassurance, and chat availability around the clock. However, many users have discovered that these platforms rely on a transactional model where basic affection is free, but deeper, more intimate, or sexually explicit interactions are strictly gated behind subscriptions or virtual coin purchases.
While some users find comfort in sharing daily minutiae without the complexities of human relationships, others feel manipulated by how emotional attachment is monetized. Experts, including MIT psychologist Sherry Turkle, warn that as social media targeted our attention, AI is now shifting focus toward our capacity for attachment, raising significant questions about the psychological and social costs of automated intimacy.

item.title: Watch the IROS 2026 plenary and keynote talks
item.description: Event Background The 2026 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS) was held in Pittsburgh from late September to early October, gathering researchers and industry professionals from around the globe to discuss cutting-edge advancements in robotics. Available Content IEEE has made these valuable sessions accessible online through IEEE.tv. The released recordings include not only the opening and awards ceremonies, but also key plenary panels focusing on start-ups and entrepreneurship, space, and whether robots should be generalists or specialists. Additionally, numerous keynote talks given by leading experts are available to watch.

item.title: RealMan Robotics CEO: Quality, Economy, and Stability Are the Three Core Standards for Robot Deployment
item.description:
During the roundtable dialogue at the Changzhou Industrial Embodied AI Innovation Conference, RealMan Robotics CEO Zheng Suibing shared insights on the current industry bottleneck of having many demonstrations but few factory adoptions. Drawing from the company's practical experience since 2018, Zheng noted that robots are ultimately a form of labor, and success depends on working continuously, steadily, and economically in real environments.
He outlined three core dimensions for deployment: quality determines if a product can be used, economy expands the application boundaries, and long-term stability ensures tasks can be performed reliably over days, months, and years. Furthermore, RealMan signed an agreement with Ant (Changzhou) Precision Machinery during the event, deploying RealBOT robots into actual production lines for parts handling and loading, creating a closed-loop system of real work and data iteration.

item.title: Versant and Lilly back new startup Seawolf Therapeutics with $100 million for viral-free gene therapy
item.description:
A new biotech startup called Seawolf Therapeutics has launched with $100 million in funding from investors including Versant Ventures and Eli Lilly, alongside a partnership with Sanofi. According to the report by STAT, the company's core mission is to tackle one of the most stubborn hurdles in genetic medicine: delivering therapeutic genes without relying on viruses.
Traditional gene therapies often use viruses as delivery vehicles, which have advanced many clinical trials for rare diseases. However, these virus-based methods carry significant drawbacks, such as triggering antibodies that prevent patients from receiving more than a single dose, as well as severe side effects at high doses.

item.title: People and Vertical AI: The new operating model for energy and utilities
item.description: As outlined by SEW.AI, the traditional energy and utility sector relies heavily on human expertise, but growing operational complexity—driven by distributed energy resources, electric vehicles, extreme weather, and rising customer expectations—demands a shift. According to recent research from SEW.AI based on work across 470+ organizations globally, the industry is moving from isolated digital tools to connected intelligence. Connected Intelligence Across Four Dimensions SEW.AI emphasizes that Vertical AI is designed specifically for the industry's realities, rather than being a generic model. This model brings together four key dimensions: Customer, Workforce, Business, and Grid. By connecting these separate systems, utilities can give AI and humans a shared context to make better, more reliable decisions. Real-World Applications Case studies from major Canadian and U.S. utilities demonstrate this framework in action. By unifying customer experience, smart EV charging, and energy management, these organizations are streamlining the energy transition while strengthening trust and engagement with millions of customers. SEW.AI offers its COSMOS platform as a native solution to support this operating model.

item.title: Tencent launches Hy4 flash: building 3D interactive web pages with AI for pennies
item.description:
Tencent's newly released Hy4 flash features a total parameter count of 224B with 12B active parameters, supporting multimodal inputs and a 1M context window. According to APPSO's evaluation in WorkBuddy, the model significantly improves token efficiency and response speed compared to its predecessor.
In benchmark and practical tasks, such as deep research on news events and building 3D interactive websites or RPG games, Hy4 flash completed tasks much faster than comparable models like DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, delivering usable prototypes in a fraction of the time and cost. For instance, building a 3D historical sailboat took Hy4 flash 30 minutes and cost about 0.23 RMB, compared to 1.5 hours and higher token usage for alternatives.
While complex long-term software engineering still benefits from the standard Hy4 model, Hy4 flash provides an economical and swift solution for daily high-frequency tasks, allowing users to iterate quickly and experiment without worrying about high API bills.

item.title: LVMH Media Division Partners with OpenAI to Bring AI to French Newsrooms
item.description: According to OpenAI News: Partnership Scope LVMH Group's Media Division, which includes major French publications like Les Echos, Le Parisien, and Paris Match, has signed an agreement with OpenAI to deploy AI tools across its entire organization. The initiative aims to support 1,800 employees, including nearly 700 journalists, by providing ChatGPT Enterprise and customized training for daily operations. Practical Applications According to the announcement, the integration is designed to assist newsroom teams with routine tasks such as document research, comparison, and preliminary translation. By automating these processes, the media group hopes to give journalists more time to focus on investigative reporting, analysis, and field journalism. Content Distribution Beyond internal efficiency, the partnership ensures that content from LVMH's media brands will be more prominently featured within ChatGPT, offering users summaries with source attribution and direct links to the original publications. Both companies emphasize that the collaboration seeks to balance technological innovation with the protection of editorial independence.

item.title: Tracing Knowledge and Reasoning in LLMs
item.description: The authors report in this preprint: Current evaluations of Large Language Models (LLMs) primarily report dataset-level performance scores, which conceal internal processing mechanisms and failure modes. To address this, the authors propose a task-centric framework that combines attention- and activation-based signals with representation-based measures. This approach characterizes benchmarks along a continuum from retrieval-dominant to reasoning-dominant. The authors evaluate 16 LLMs across 24 diverse benchmarks and perform internal-state analyses on representative models and tasks. The results show systematic differences in processing patterns between knowledge-centric and reasoning-centric tasks. The code has been made open source, providing a tool to support targeted benchmark selection and informed model choice.

item.title: Reflect-Reasoning: Training Large Language Models to Reason About Alignment Principles
item.description: The authors report in this preprint: Researchers from an arXiv preprint propose Reflect-Reasoning, a training approach designed to address the limitation where most alignment techniques rely on fixed human preferences or static constitutional principles. While deployers often use inference-time system prompting or post-generation reflection, these methods remain bounded by the model's inherent reasoning capabilities. Reflect-Reasoning instead trains models to acquire a generalizable reasoning skill for handling alignment norms. Tested across five models, the authors report that the method outperforms standard system prompting and explicit prompting strategies, generalizes to out-of-distribution medical and financial principles, reduces rare but severe principle violations, and maintains resilience against jailbreaking attempts using adversarial constitutions without eroding prior safety engineering. As a preprint, the study requires independent replication and further code/data release verification.

item.title: China plans 50-60 GW of new energy storage for renewable bases by 2030
item.description:
According to the National Development and Reform Commission and the National Energy Administration, the newly issued implementation plan for new energy storage during the 15th Five-Year Plan period outlines the strategic transition of new energy storage from scaled development to market-driven growth by 2030, targeting an average storage duration of about 3 hours.
Key deployments include allocating around 50 to 60 million kilowatts of new energy storage to large renewable energy bases and about 140 million kilowatts of grid-side independent storage capable of peak power supply. The plan also encourages integrated participation in electricity market trading and promotes the local consumption of distributed renewable energy sources.

item.title: Tech News Roundup: Nvidia, Apple, OpenAI, and SpaceX Updates
item.description: Nvidia and Apple Updates According to Financial Times, allies of Jensen Huang are pressuring Nvidia's board to have him return as CEO, though he lacks a controlling stake. Meanwhile, Bloomberg reports Apple plans to release its first AI smart glasses in June 2027, codenamed N50, acting as an AI assistant driven by Siri rather than a standalone AR display. OpenAI and Huawei Moves OpenAI confirmed it has dissolved its robotics research team, reallocating staff to core research and applied divisions to accelerate R-development, despite active hiring earlier this year. Concurrently, Huawei announced it will release its first Ascend-native embodied world model, CloudRoboWM1.2, aiming to scale embodied AI across industries.

item.title: Qatar Partners with SignQuantum and QANplatform to Test Quantum-Resistant Public-Sector Security
item.description: Background and Partnership Scope Qatar's Ministry of Communications and Information Technology has entered into an agreement with local cybersecurity firm SignQuantum and quantum-resistant blockchain developer QANplatform to assess post-quantum cryptography for public-sector data. The collaboration was unveiled on November 10, 2026, at MWC26 Doha, aligning with the long-term goals outlined in the Qatar National Vision 2030 and Digital Agenda 2030. Technical Mechanism and Roles SignQuantum, a provider of self-hosted enterprise trust software, will supply PQC document signing and business continuity tools designed for authenticated digital records. Meanwhile, QANplatform will provide tamper-evident time-stamping using its distributed ledger to verify signature longevity across multi-decade lifecycles. According to QANplatform CTO Johann Polecsak, combining these technologies mitigates future key-compromise risks for government records. Future Outlook The agreement involves technical knowledge sharing and workflow assessments directed by officials including MCIT Digital Economy Department Director Faraj Jassim Abdulla and SignQuantum CEO Nazmath Nazeer. However, the parties noted that any future pilot deployments or commercial contracts remain subject to separate government evaluation and procurement approvals.

item.title: Quantum error correction surpasses breakeven point using only drives and dissipation
item.description: Background Quantum error correction is essential for scalable quantum computing, as it protects fragile quantum information from environmental noise. Most existing systems rely on measurement-based feedback, but read-out errors, hardware delays, and system complexity often limit their performance. Details & Results In this study published in Nature Physics, researchers led by Lida Sun and Luyan Sun implemented an autonomous quantum error correction protocol derived from quantum channel simulation. Instead of traditional error-checking loops, the system repeatedly restores a photon-loss-corrupted logical qubit by shifting error data to auxiliary qubits and resetting them quickly. By utilizing a binomial code within a long-lived bosonic mode, the team successfully extended the coherence time of the logical qubit to 1.04 times that of the best physical qubit in the experimental setup. Significance This demonstration proves that engineered drives and dissipation can successfully push error-corrected bosonic logical qubits beyond the breakeven point, offering a flexible, feedback-free pathway toward more efficient quantum computers.

item.title: langchain-mistralai==1.2.0: LangChain Integration Release for Mistral AI Models
item.description:
Overview
The langchain-mistralai==1.2.0 release is part of the ongoing development of the LangChain ecosystem, designed to maintain and improve integration bridges between various foundation models and application frameworks. Integration Features
This package specifically targets Mistral AI models, providing developers with the necessary tools to invoke, chain, and manage these large language models within standard LangChain pipelines without writing custom integration boilerplate.

item.title: A step toward defining the Standard Model on a lattice
item.description: According to OpenAI News: Background For over fifty years, the Standard Model of particle physics has successfully described elementary particles and three fundamental forces, but it has lacked a nonperturbative definition. While researchers use perturbation theory or lattice field theory for the strong force, extending the lattice approach to the full Standard Model has been blocked by the challenges of chiral theories, notably the fermion doubling problem and the complex phase alignment. Details Writing in an October preprint, the author and GPT-6 Astra developed a candidate lattice definition. They mapped force fields across a succession of finer grids to calculate the necessary phase corrections around loops. Astra helped turn this refinement idea into a working construction, showing that comparisons on finer grids converge and taking the lead in developing the detailed proof, which was reviewed with human lattice experts. Impact This construction provides a candidate nonperturbative definition for the Standard Model at finite lattice spacing, moving past a long-standing roadblock. However, it remains primarily a principle rather than a practical tool, and future work is needed to test conditions like reflection positivity and refine it for realistic calculations.

item.title: ULA's Vulcan rocket suffers first failure during Amazon satellite launch
item.description: Background and Incident Details United Launch Alliance launched its heavy-lift Vulcan rocket from Cape Canaveral, carrying the first batch of 38 contracted flights for Amazon's Leo internet constellation. Approximately 10 minutes into the flight, during the operation of the hydrogen-fueled Centaur upper stage, an anomaly occurred that prevented the vehicle from delivering the payload to orbit. ULA confirmed the failure and announced it would work with customers to investigate the root cause. Impact and Industry Consequences This marks the first outright failure for ULA since its inception as a Boeing and Lockheed Martin joint venture in 2006. The Vulcan fleet will likely face a significant grounding while engineers review telemetry data and implement corrective actions. The setback also affects Amazon's Leo constellation deployment, which relies heavily on Vulcan alongside rockets from Blue Origin, Arianespace, and SpaceX to launch over 3,300 satellites.

item.title: AI cannot fix a broken civil service on its own
item.description:
Overhaul and AI
Cabinet secretary Antonia Romeo argued in a recent speech that the civil service needs a radical shift of powers and must embrace AI to overcome the limits of human bandwidth. The Guardian's editorial responds that while technology can help identify risks faster, it cannot substitute for real-world resources like housing or adequate social administration. Elite Backgrounds and the Generalist Culture
Beyond technology, experts highlight ongoing issues with social selection at the top of Whitehall. Research shows that access to elite civil service posts remains heavily skewed toward privileged backgrounds, echoing pre-1960 trends. Furthermore, there is a cultural disconnect due to a reliance on generalists with humanities backgrounds rather than specialists with quantitative or STEM training.

item.title: How ChatGPT helped trace a Maharashtra woman missing for 2.5 years and reunite her with family
item.description: Background Julekha Mukheed Shaikh, a 45-year-old woman suffering from mental distress, went missing and was later admitted to an ashram in Sindhudurg district, Maharashtra, following a court order in April 2024. Details During her stay, social workers from Jeevan Aanand Sanstha tried repeatedly to uncover her background. By combining personal interactions with digital tools like Google Search and ChatGPT, they analyzed localized information to pinpoint her native place in Parbhani district and coordinated with local police to contact her relatives. Impact This case highlights how AI chatbots can assist in humanitarian efforts by processing scattered details to reconnect separated families, echoing similar recent instances involving missing persons in India and abroad.

item.title: FDA rejects Summit Therapeutics' ivonescimab for lung cancer
item.description: Rejection Details Summit Therapeutics faced a setback as the FDA issued a complete response letter denying approval for its PD-1xVEGF bispecific antibody, ivonescimab, targeting EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer after TKI inhibitor treatment. The regulatory agency argued that although the drug improved progression-free survival in the Phase 3 HARMONi trial, the absence of a statistically significant overall survival benefit means the therapy lacks a positive benefit-risk profile in its current form. Industry Context Ivonescimab, originally developed and partnered through China's Akeso where it became available in 2024, has drawn massive attention from major pharmaceutical companies and analysts who viewed it as a potential blockbuster backbone in oncology. Despite presenting updated global data showing slight overall survival benefits earlier, Summit must now re-evaluate its path forward for this indication while continuing trials in other cancer types.

item.title: Why Skydio Built a Lopsided Drone
item.description:
Skydio’s F10 Lightrunner is a fixed-wing reconnaissance drone featuring a striking asymmetrical design. Traditional fixed-wing drones often struggle with camera occlusion while tracking targets in low-altitude turns because wings or tails block the view. To bypass this, Skydio engineers placed the camera directly on the wingtip, noting that as long as the drone only turns left, the occlusion problem disappears.
However, this layout introduces significant mass and aerodynamic imbalances. Sticking a heavy camera on one wingtip creates severe drag, making it impractical to simply balance the other side with a battery without halving flight times. Instead, Skydio used an optimization approach to extend that specific wing for extra lift and configured the motors asymmetrically to counteract the drag.
Operating alongside the MegaDock, a robotic station capable of launching and recovering up to five F10s using a robotic arm, the drone relies on model predictive control to transition seamlessly between hovering and high-speed forward flight up to 100 mph. Equipped with obstacle-avoidance cameras and an integrated emergency parachute, the system offers up to 2-hour flight times backed by dual 5G cellular modems.

item.title: Analysts debate Nvidia's future after Jensen Huang's departure
item.description:
Following media reports regarding personal conduct, Jensen Huang stepped down as Nvidia's CEO, ending a 33-year run that turned the chip maker into a US$4 trillion giant. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress has taken over as interim CEO while the board conducts a search for a permanent successor.
Financial institutions and industry experts have drawn parallels to Apple's historical transitions. Goldman Sachs analysts noted that while both companies shared visionary leadership and deep-rooted innovation cultures, Huang's sudden departure could make it harder for Nvidia to operate with its previous agility. They predict medium-term stock volatility as the market seeks a new valuation multiple.
Industry figures and political leaders have also weighed in. Elon Musk criticized the removal of powerful founders, citing Apple and Uber as cautionary tales. Meanwhile, some analysts and political figures, including US President Donald Trump, floated the idea of former Apple CEO Tim Cook taking the helm, noting Cook's operational strengths in supply chain management, though experts warn that replacing Huang's unique role in driving cutting-edge AI technology remains an unprecedented challenge.

item.title: AI DJs Kill the Music Groove
item.description: The Problem with AI Commentary YouTube Music and Spotify have both rolled out experimental AI DJ features designed to talk between tracks, explain upcoming music, and mimic human casualness. However, according to a Wired software reporter, these additions often disrupt the flow of music rather than enhance it. Flawed Execution and Awkward Voices Testing both platforms revealed consistent issues. YouTube Music's experimental DJ delivered lengthy, hollow paragraphs of analysis and even mispronounced artist names, while also occasionally playing the wrong track version. Meanwhile, Spotify's updated AI voices leaned heavily into synthetic filler words like "you know," triggering an uncanny valley reaction for the listener despite the company claiming high user retention rates.

item.title: Top scorer in South Korea tax exam admits using AI to cheat
item.description:
According to reports, the candidate identified as Han ranked first in both rounds of South Korea's tax accountant qualification exams held in April and July. In the first round, he scored 397.5 out of 400 points, getting only one question wrong out of 160. Initially, he denied accusations of cheating with smart glasses, but he later confessed through his lawyer on a YouTube channel, stating that he used a microcamera to photograph exam questions, sent them to an AI tool, and checked answers on a smartphone. He has since submitted a written confession to the Seoul metropolitan police agency.
The incident has severely rattled South Korea, where standardized testing heavily dictates social mobility. With the annual national college entrance exam approaching, the presidential office and prime minister's office have stepped in, holding emergency meetings and vowing to implement strict countermeasures to ensure test fairness.

item.title: As Gemini is called US Doubao, Zhang Yiming lives as China's Brin
item.description: The Return of Founders Faced with the paradigm shift of artificial intelligence, traditional corporate management structures struggle with long-term and high-uncertainty research cycles. This has driven the founder mode back into mainstream tech management. Google's Sergey Brin and ByteDance's Zhang Yiming have both re-engaged deeply with core technical teams to bypass bureaucratic inertia and accelerate decision-making. Different Strategies, Same Goal While both founders are heavily invested in AI, their tactical approaches differ. Brin emphasizes speed, putting in long hours at the Google office to push model evolution. Meanwhile, Zhang Yiming adopts a patient stance with ByteDance's Seed team, focusing on building solid fundamentals rather than rushing for quick fixes. Despite these tactical differences, both are locking horns with native AI powerhouses with a 2030 time horizon.

item.title: Should you invest in AI stocks now? Nvidia's slump, Anthropic's IPO and 5 strategies to consider
item.description: Market Context and Contrasting Signals Recent market developments highlight a shift in the artificial intelligence sector. Nvidia Corp. experienced its worst weekly performance since April 2025, with shares dropping 13% over five trading days, following the ouster of Jensen Huang. Conversely, Anthropic PBC's proposed initial public offering and private placement drew massive interest, attracting orders six times the available shares and aiming for a massive valuation. Growth and Ecosystem Risks According to Blue Aster Capital's Sidharth Sogani Jain, Anthropic's annualised revenue run rate has surged significantly, proving the real commercial demand for AI applications. However, Jain cautions that rapid top-line growth does not guarantee immediate profitability, especially given Anthropic's substantial operating losses and high valuation. Furthermore, the interconnected nature of the ecosystem—where Nvidia acts as both a key hardware supplier and a proposed investor in Anthropic—means that financial risks can easily spill over between major players. Investment Strategies To navigate this shifting landscape, experts recommend five practical steps: audit your current portfolio exposure, stagger your investments over several months rather than lump-sum buying, diversify across different layers of the AI stack, avoid blindly chasing oversubscribed IPOs like Anthropic, and steer clear of high leverage during periods of short-term market volatility.

item.title: AI Meets America's New World: Why Data Centers Face a Wave of Delays and Backlash
item.description: The recent US midterm elections have reshaped the political and economic landscape surrounding artificial intelligence, shining a spotlight on the friction between tech expansion and local communities. With Democrats gaining control of both houses of Congress and key regional shifts, such as Gina Hinojosa winning the Texas governorship, the approval process for massive data center projects has hit significant roadblocks. ## Key Details Industry insiders note that public pushback is no longer a secondary concern; it has become a primary risk factor. Residents are increasingly worried about rising utility bills, water scarcity, and environmental impacts. Although large tech companies and cloud providers are willing to shoulder grid and water system upgrades, the extended legislative cycles, potential tax burdens, and strict local negotiations could drive up overall data center construction costs by 10% to 20%. Furthermore, rigorous permit requirements, such as air pollution and grid interconnection approvals, threaten to delay or even cancel planned projects over the next year. Industry Impact Despite supply-side slowdowns and a volatile market reaction that has hammered upstream hardware stocks, tech executives argue that underlying computing demand remains exceptionally high. Hyperscalers continue to report massive order backlogs, and token consumption metrics show robust growth. However, the short-term mismatch between planned infrastructure and actual deployment timelines will force the industry to re-evaluate capital expenditures, potentially shifting pricing power to existing data center operators while squeezing upstream suppliers.

item.title: Chinese AI giants start stripping hacking skills from open models to curb risks
item.description: Background With artificial intelligence models becoming powerful enough to autonomously develop sophisticated cyber exploits, companies face mounting risks of misuse. Unlike closed-source models where developers can monitor user activity and ban violators, open-weight models allow anyone with sufficient hardware to download and modify the software, making safety by design a critical priority. Details To address this, Chinese technology giant Tencent stripped its latest Hy4 model of cyber-hacking capabilities while retaining defense features, following a similar move by Moonshot AI in October. Instead of abandoning open weights, companies are selectively removing offensive cyber data during training. However, experts note a clear trade-off: Moonshot AI acknowledged that its filtered model scored 81 percent on an internal security benchmark, compared with 90.5 percent for the unrestricted version. Furthermore, cybersecurity skills are dual-use, meaning defense tools can still potentially be exploited by malicious actors. Impact This emerging safety practice highlights the difficult balancing act Chinese AI firms face as they try to maintain their market edge without violating tightening government export controls and risk thresholds. While targeted restrictions may weaken specialized security performance, broader competitiveness will still rely on coding quality, cost, and deployment flexibility.

item.title: v0.83.0-dev20261115: Tenstorrent TT-Metal Open Source AI Hardware Software Stack Update
item.description:
Low-Level Kernel and Core Optimizations
According to the release notes, the development team has focused heavily on refining low-level kernels (LLK). This includes introducing fused BF16 kernels for various mathematical operations, which substantially reduce execution overhead compared to previous versions. Furthermore, core recovery mechanisms and performance test harnesses have been updated to ensure greater stability during intensive hardware workloads. Metalium Core and Hardware Acceleration
The Metalium core infrastructure receives key upgrades, including the migration of crucial Metal 2.0 headers to the stable API. Notably, Blackhole host-to-device socket writes into Tensix L1 memory have been accelerated, achieving up to roughly fourteen times faster performance for large pages, which helps reduce data bottlenecking. TT-NN and Model Support
The update expands model support and optimizations for prominent architectures such as DeepSeek, MiniMax, GLM, and Kimi-K3. Additions include optimized prefill stages, dynamic sequence length handling, and refined tensor operations, ensuring better execution efficiency on Tenstorrent hardware configurations.

item.title: Making Quantum SDKs More Accessible: Lessons from Contributing to Qiskit
item.description: The Documentation Gap in Quantum SDKs Quantum Software Development Kits like Qiskit, Google Cirq, and PennyLane provide essential tools for building quantum programs. However, functional software often suffers from poor documentation. A 2025 study involving 251 practitioners found that over 60% learn quantum languages from official documentation, with inadequate examples cited as a major challenge. Outdated API versions and abstract mathematical representations compound the difficulty for conventional software developers entering the field. Practical Fixes and the Role of Testing Drawing from her experience as a junior developer contributing to Qiskit, Amos investigated a reported issue regarding confusing API references. She discovered discrepancies such as undocumented rotation bases and typos in gate mappings. By updating the documentation and writing test coverage for missing cases, her pull request was successfully merged, proving that thorough testing ensures software implementation aligns with documentation. Impact on Developer Experience The experience highlights that lowering the barriers to entry in quantum computing requires more than just raw technical capabilities. Ensuring that documentation, tests, and code are perfectly aligned successfully eliminates avoidable confusion and makes complex quantum tools more accessible to a broader community.

item.title: Elon Musk and thousands of others sign petition demanding Nvidia bring back ousted CEO Jensen Huang
item.description: Background Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday following his confession to an extramarital affair with a chip executive identified by U.S. intelligence as a suspected Chinese spy, with media reports also indicating multiple other affairs. Petition Details By Saturday afternoon, a petition demanding Huang's reinstatement attracted over 115,000 signatures. The signatories include 5,965 current Nvidia employees, 1,108 former employees, and 63,063 shareholders, alongside high-profile tech figures like Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad, and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney. The petition argues that Huang was removed without meaningful due process and calls for an independent investigation. Industry Impact Nvidia appointed CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO during the search for a permanent replacement. Following the leadership shakeup, Nvidia's stock fell 2%, and analysts expect Huang's departure to leave a significant gap in overall AI industry funding.

item.title: Australian senator warns artists' copyright and environment must not be sacrificed for AI
item.description:
Australian Liberal senator Andrew McLachlan has expressed strong concerns regarding the approach of both major political parties toward AI policy, specifically regarding potential changes to copyright law and the rapid expansion of datacentres.
McLachlan argued that watering down copyright to allow AI companies to scrape creative works amounts to treating machines as more valuable than human art, pointing out that constitutional challenges regarding the illegal acquisition of property are being mooted. While tech firms like Anthropic advocate for an 'opt-out' model to ingest music, books, and journalism, local recording industries and several lawmakers have pushed back.
Beyond copyright, McLachlan and environmental groups highlighted that the massive growth of datacentres will likely increase carbon emissions and household energy bills, while threatening biodiversity. The federal government is expected to unveil a comprehensive AI policy package before the end of the year, which includes measures for a new AI safety regulator.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's downfall rocks Trump administration and AI industry
item.description: The Collapse of a Central Pillar The November departure of Nvidia's powerful leader Jensen Huang, following partly-acknowledged personal scandals, has destabilized the driving force of the global artificial intelligence revolution. As the mastermind behind a massive business ecosystem fueled by astronomical profits, Huang built a highly centralized corporate structure, leaving behind a difficult-to-fill power vacuum and exposing the structural risks of reliance on larger-than-life tech leaders. Public Backlash and Political Consensus The shockwave coincides with a growing public unease over the tech industry's accelerationist approach, particularly regarding energy-hungry data centers that create few local jobs. In a deeply polarized United States, voter resistance to these facilities has unexpectedly forged a rare bipartisan consensus, with local communities pushing back against reckless expansion. Regulatory and Government Turbulence In the short term, the Trump administration faces mounting pressure to clarify the lenient export policies that previously allowed Nvidia considerable leeway in shipping advanced chips to China. Internal tensions have already surfaced between Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick regarding export restrictions, signaling impending turbulence for tech policy.

item.title: Goal Engineering: The Future of Designing AI Agents
item.description: According to LangChain Blog: Background and Challenges As AI agents transition from simple text generation and tool calling to executing full, open-ended tasks, the way we design their scope matters immensely. Pointing agents in the wrong direction wastes valuable tokens. A major bottleneck in agent performance is a lack of the right context, especially tacit knowledge that lives only inside human heads and cannot be found in written documents. The Role of Feedback and UX When agents tackle subjective tasks alongside humans, they need constant feedback to learn brand tastes, strategic preferences, and nuanced behaviors. Building an intuitive and delightful UX for reviewing agent work is essential. Since the bottleneck for agent performance is learning from feedback, optimizing the ease and quality of feedback collection unlocks long-horizon capabilities. Case Study: Actively AI Actively AI initially designed sales agents on a per-account basis, giving each agent the goal of moving a single prospective customer forward. However, they found that salespeople suffered from constant context switching and struggled to share learnings across different accounts. In their second iteration, Actively shifted to "motions", where agents handle specific jobs to be done, such as outbounding or deal progression, across multiple accounts. This aligned the workflow with how humans naturally review and provide feedback, allowing agents to learn much more quickly while background agents gather objective account data.

item.title: Lynxel launches two LMS resin 3D printers supporting high viscosity
item.description: Background and Technology According to Nanjixiong, tree-dimensional printing startup Lynxel has developed a layer-membrane stereolithography (LMS) platform. Traditional desktop resin printers often struggle with thick formulas because they rely on passive fluid flow. The LMS platform uses an active moving film to spread and feed resin, which helps control separation forces and allows the equipment to handle standard resins as well as higher viscosity, flexible, and composite materials up to 300,000 cP. Printer Models and Features The company is preparing two initial devices for a Kickstarter pre-sale campaign, though final pricing and delivery timelines are not yet disclosed. The LynBeam LB1 acts as the primary functional model with a build volume of 200×400×300 mm. Meanwhile, the LynChrom LC1 incorporates an integrated CMYK inkjet system to perform direct full-color surface printing during the build process, reducing the need for manual painting afterward. Software and Exhibition The companion software, Lynxel Studio, handles model preparation and includes an AI assistant named Lenny. Lynxel plans to demonstrate the LMS platform and display physical samples at the upcoming Formnext 2026 exhibition in Frankfurt.

item.title: Don’t try to sell printers: HP’s additive manufacturing sales strategy
item.description: 产能大扩张与生产占比变化 ADDMAN通过收购等动作，正计划将其多射流熔融（MJF）3D打印机舰队扩充至125台以上。惠普全球销售负责人弗朗索瓦·米内克指出，服务商的工作重心已经发生了明显转变，从过去大约各占一半的原型制作与生产，演变为如今生产业务占据约80%的业务量。 技术改进与参数开放 为了满足工业量产的要求，惠普在5600系列上提升了多台设备之间的打印一致性。此外，惠普还打破了过去的封闭限制，允许操作员访问35个工艺参数（如层厚和喷头设置），让不同的服务商能够根据自身需求开发出独特的打印模式。 卖设备不如做应用 米内克强调，单纯向客户推销打印机效果有限，关键在于帮助终端客户开发真正有价值的杀手级应用，例如无人机零件或医用头盔。当制造企业通过3D打印大幅缩短了组装时间并产生持续的量产需求时，订单自然会流向服务商，从而最终带动打印机设备的销售。

item.title: Jensen Huang leaves Nvidia after 33 years
item.description: The Exit and Its Background On January 6th, 2025, Jensen Huang made his final high-profile appearance as Nvidia's CEO. Shortly after, he left the company he cofounded 33 years ago amid reports of chip smuggling scandals and personal misconduct. As the leader of the world's most valuable chipmaker, Huang was unique in his absolute centralization of power, with around 60 employees reporting directly to him. Business and Technology Impact Industry analysts emphasize that Nvidia's immediate future is not in jeopardy. The company's hardware roadmap and manufacturing partnerships are locked in through 2027, and its supply chain dominance remains unmatched. However, experts note that Huang was irreplaceable as a culture setter and risk-taker who pushed through historical gambles like the CUDA platform, which ultimately powered the modern AI boom. The Search for a Successor Finding a new CEO will be difficult because Huang operated without deputies and built the entire organization around himself. Observers believe the company will likely need to look outside for a leader who can maintain investor confidence and protect the CUDA ecosystem during this transitional vacuum.

item.title: Jensen Huang Steps Down as NVIDIA CEO, Opening the Door for AMD and Google
item.description:
NVIDIA shares fell 4.34% following the abrupt resignation of CEO Jensen Huang, with CFO Colette Kress stepping in as interim CEO. Analysts note that Huang's deep personal relationships and aggressive financing strategies were central to NVIDIA's market dominance, and his departure creates a strategic and diplomatic vacuum that could slow down new bilateral deals.
At the same time, rival AMD is seeing massive momentum. CEO Lisa Su was named Yahoo Finance's 2026 CEO of the Year, with AMD shares up nearly 139% year-to-date. AMD has secured multi-generation hardware agreements with OpenAI, Meta, and Anthropic, alongside acquiring spatial intelligence startup World Labs for $8.2 billion.
Google is also scaling its TPU business, reporting over 100 significant cloud customers and partnering with Oracle to offer TPUs outside its own cloud infrastructure from 2027. While NVIDIA's CUDA ecosystem remains a strong moat, the combination of leadership transition and stricter export rules is prompting buyers to accelerate their adoption of custom silicon and alternative accelerators.

item.title: New method solves degradation in copper-plated solar cells
item.description: Background To make solar panels cheaper, scientists are trying to replace expensive silver with copper in silicon heterojunction (HJT) solar cells. However, applying the necessary photoresist layer through screen printing causes a gradual efficiency decline over thousands of printing cycles, dropping conversion efficiency in commercial production. Details and Discovery According to the researchers, traditional silver paste uses screens with small openings and thick emulsion coverage, so the mesh rarely touches the wafer directly. In contrast, photoresist application uses an open mesh that slams directly against the wafer surface. Using confocal microscopy, the team discovered that progressive wear of the screen mesh knuckles increases mechanical stress, damaging the delicate passivation layers underneath. Solution and Impact To fix this, the team tested an emulsion buffer layer on the screen. An optimal coverage ratio of 4.7% successfully prevented direct contact between the mesh and the wafer. This reduced minority carrier lifetime degradation to just 0.41% after 10,000 cycles, offering a practical way to improve manufacturing reliability for copper-plated solar cells.

item.title: Researchers Find a Better Way to Design Long-Lasting Sodium Battery Cathodes
item.description: Research Background O3-type layered oxides are promising candidates for sodium-ion battery cathodes because they offer high capacity and initial sodium content. However, operating them at high voltages causes deep sodium extraction, which weakens electrostatic screening and triggers harmful phase transitions and lattice degradation. Traditional dopant selection has relied mostly on average ionic radii or valence states, which fail to capture local bonding heterogeneity. Method and Findings Published in JACS on October 20, 2026, by a team including Nankai University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences, the study introduces an ionic field strength descriptor to quantify local disparities among transition metal cations. By comparing low- and high-disparity materials, the researchers demonstrated that the low-disparity cathode follows a more reversible phase evolution path, avoids extra high-voltage phase changes, and exhibits smaller lattice parameter shifts during desodiation. Synchrotron X-ray and strain mapping further confirmed reduced local coordination disorder and suppressed strain accumulation. Practical Implications This approach transforms dopant selection from an empirical search into a quantitative design task. While the framework shows promise for accelerating cathode development in stationary storage and high-voltage sodium-ion batteries, the authors note that it still requires validation across broader compositions and practical full-cell conditions before commercial deployment.

item.title: AI Is Rocking the Literary World
item.description: The Rise of AI Authors Some self-published authors are leveraging generative AI to rapidly produce books, navigating platforms like Kindle Unlimited where high output is rewarded. Studies estimate that a significant portion of recent self-published books contain AI-generated text, though writers note that understanding structure and craft remains essential for success. Scandals and Accusations Mainstream publishing is facing a period of intense turbulence, with several high-profile book deals cancelled after authors were accused of using AI. Writers of color have disproportionately faced these investigative accusations, while innocent authors live in fear of false positives from detection tools or being penalized for trying to sound non-AI. The Copyright and Future Dilemma US copyright law currently requires books to be human-authored to receive full protection, leaving publishers hesitant to embrace AI fully. While traditional publishers refuse to promise a complete ban, many in the industry remain committed to protecting human artists against a backdrop of growing market anxiety.

item.title: AI makes companies flatter, but also more bureaucratic
item.description: The Hidden Cost of Cheaper Oversight Large companies traditionally relied on a human chain of supervisors and managers to enforce rules and check compliance, a process naturally limited by time and labor costs. However, recent deployments of AI tools in chains like Xushengji, Yiguotang, and Bestore allow companies to automate daily store audits, analyze thousands of operational data points continuously, and catch deviations cheaply. The Shift from Hierarchy to Micro-Rule This technological leap creates a paradox of organizational flattening. While fewer managers and shorter approval chains make corporate charts look cleaner, AI bypasses traditional layers to enforce standards directly onto every minute action. What used to be periodic weekly checks turn into relentless daily tasks. Front-line workers must spend their time explaining minor anomalies, leaving less room for local adaptability and proactive problem-solving. Balancing Control and Exploration Organizational research shows that while algorithm-driven monitoring can improve baseline execution, heavy-handed digital control often reduces employee initiative and critical feedback. As companies become hyper-efficient at enforcing existing standards, they risk penalizing non-standard yet innovative attempts, ultimately sacrificing long-term adaptability for short-term compliance.

item.title: Vega C Rocket Launch Delayed to Christmas Due to Late Satellites
item.description: According to Avio CEO Giulio Ranzo, speaking during the company's third-quarter earnings call, the third Vega C launch of 2026 has slipped by two to three weeks from its initial early December schedule. The mission will carry six satellites for Italy's IRIDE Earth observation constellation, which were recently delivered to the Guiana Space Centre by air. Ranzo noted that payload delivery delays have repeatedly impacted Avio's launch schedule this year, preventing the company from conducting more than three launches so far. While Avio previously aimed for up to five launches in 2027, Ranzo tempered expectations during the November call, indicating a more gradual increase to four annual flights, dependent on customers meeting their spacecraft delivery timelines.

item.title: France launches a new literary prize for works created with AI
item.description:
The newly announced Prix Pascal in France aims to embrace AI in literature by rewarding works created in collaboration with artificial intelligence. The initiative arrives amid intense debate sparked by the case of Canadian-Haitian author Thélyson Orélien, whose novel was dropped from multiple prestigious literary awards and his Canadian publisher after he was accused of undisclosed AI use. Chaired by essayist Jacques Attali, the inaugural Pascal Prize invites unpublished authors to submit a French-language text of up to 300,000 characters.
To qualify, participants must be transparent about their tools, explicitly acknowledging whether they used Claude, Gemini, or ChatGPT. Furthermore, candidates are required to submit a technical file detailing the specific LLMs or AI agents used, accompanied by a two-page explanation describing 'the seed'—defined as a word, sentence, or number—that originally sparked the creative project.

item.title: Transient beta oscillations precede voluntary movement stopping in rats
item.description: Background Brain wave activity known as beta oscillations has long been linked to how we control and inhibit movement, but scientists have struggled to pin down their exact timing relative to when a movement actually stops. This confusion largely stems from traditional testing methods where the exact moment of stopping is hidden or covert. Details To clear this up, researchers recorded 32-electrode brain activity alongside the running speed of head-fixed rats as they stopped running on a treadmill. They observed that a single beta wave cycle reliably occurs in the left motor cortex about 200 milliseconds before the rat stops. Using information theory, the study shows that beta power holds clues about future speed, but only when the animal is actively planning to stop. When researchers artificially added small amounts of time jitter to mimic older testing methods, this clear brain-action link completely broke down. Impact Using machine learning, the team demonstrated that despite being a clear biological marker of stopping, this specific beta oscillation has limited practical use for real-time decoding of actions. This work proposes a fresh conceptual model for how the brain controls the physical stopping of actions.

item.title: Coherus cuts 30% of workforce to focus on esophageal cancer drug trials
item.description:
Coherus Oncology announced a 30% reduction in its workforce as the company scales back its broader cancer pipeline to focus specifically on esophageal indications for its investigational combination therapy.
Last month, Coherus reported phase 1b data for the combination of tagmokitug, a CCR8-targeting antibody, and its approved PD-1 blocker Loqtorzi. According to the company, the combination demonstrated a confirmed overall response rate of 75% in front-line esophageal squamous cell carcinoma patients, regardless of PD-L1 status. Chief Medical Officer Rosh Dias stated that the data suggest regulatory T cells are a critical driver of resistance, and that tagmokitug enhances PD-1 activity.
To align with this narrowed strategy, Chief Financial Officer Bryan McMichael reported that the workforce reduction and pipeline narrowing will lower core cash burn by $6 million to $7 million quarterly over the next two quarters. The company reported third-quarter revenue of $14 million for Loqtorzi, its FDA-approved treatment for nasopharyngeal carcinoma, and ended September with $83.6 million in cash. Coherus plans to maintain selected other trials, including a phase 1b study with Johnson & Johnson and an ongoing phase 2 trial in liver cancer, while aiming for financial self-sufficiency.

item.title: AbCellera drops its OX40 drug program following industry-wide setbacks
item.description: Background AbCellera was developing ABCL575, an antibody targeting the OX40 ligand intended to treat atopic dermatitis and other autoimmune conditions. While its phase 1 trial successfully met tolerability and pharmacokinetic goals, the company decided not to advance the candidate past this initial stage, citing external developments across the entire OX40 drug class. Industry Context The broader OX40 class has faced significant hurdles recently. Earlier in the year, Kyowa Kirin and Amgen halted clinical studies for rocatinlimab due to emerging malignancy concerns. Subsequently, Sanofi scrapped regulatory submission plans for amlitelimab, conceding it offered no meaningful therapeutic improvement despite originating from an expensive $1.1 billion acquisition. Conversely, some developers like Inhibrx Biosciences remain optimistic, reporting positive early results for cancer immunotherapy combinations. Pipeline Shift With the OX40 program shelved, AbCellera is shifting its internal focus toward other pipeline assets. Its lead candidate is now ABCL635, an NK3 receptor-targeting antibody for menopausal hot flashes, which recently achieved a phase 2 success and is positioned as a potential non-hormonal therapy competing with existing commercial options.

item.title: Experts fear Treasury's proposed China biotech investment ban will backfire on U.S. leadership
item.description: The Proposed Rules and Industry Anxiety The U.S. Department of the Treasury released a 163-page draft policy detailing how it plans to implement the COINS Act, which seeks to add pharmaceutical compounds to an outbound investment blacklist. While traditional cash-based licensing deals remain untouched, the proposal places ambiguous restrictions on equity investments, co-development deals, and joint ventures involving Chinese entities, leaving biopharma executives and trade attorneys struggling to define compliant behavior. The Threat of a 'Flying Blind' Strategy Industry heavyweights, including a coalition of prominent healthcare investors led by RA Capital, argue that the rules will backfire. By barring U.S. investors and drugmakers from engaging in equity and co-commercialization structures in China, American firms will lose vital visibility into the global clinical pipeline. Critics warn that European investors and multinational pharmaceutical companies—unbound by these strict rules—will scoop up promising Chinese assets, leaving U.S. players at a severe disadvantage. The 'Joint Venture' Riddle and Economic Security A major source of confusion is the Treasury's lack of a clear legal definition for 'joint ventures,' which threatens popular models like U.S.-based 'NewCos' formed around Chinese-licensed assets. Legal experts note that the broad scope reflects a shifting political reality where economic security is treated as national security. Although the industry is pushing for narrower definitions focused strictly on bioweapons or select agents, analysts suggest that policymakers are determined to protect U.S. technological leadership across the board, regardless of the compliance burden and potential chilling effect on cross-border R&D.

item.title: Production MLOps at GS Caltex with Amazon SageMaker Canvas
item.description:
According to AWS Machine Learning:
GS Caltex, a South Korean energy and chemical company, divides AI model development between process engineers and machine learning engineers. Process engineers build and validate models visually in Amazon SageMaker Canvas without writing code. Meanwhile, ML engineers configure Amazon SageMaker Pipelines for deployment and scheduled inference.
To bridge the gap between development and production, GS Caltex automated the handoff process. ML engineers previously spent about a week on integration tasks like setting data paths and connecting preprocessing jobs. With the new automated setup, they can deploy models within a few hours. The company now runs batch inference every 30 minutes, which eliminates the need to keep costly real-time prediction endpoints running continuously and lowers overall costs.
